drivers: US futures are modestly higher (S&P 500 +0.4%, Nasdaq-100 +0.6%) after Monday's chip-led rally (Nasdaq-100 +1.1%), with semis again firm (SOXX +1.8%, MU +2.3%, AVGO +3.3%) and AI financing in focus: Anthropic's S-1 showed $1.16B of first-half revenue (+1,304% y/y), Meta's equity raise grew to up to $97.5B with Nvidia committing $3B and AMD/Broadcom indicating interest. Oil is slightly lower (WTI ~$101) on hopes for US–Iran diplomacy, though Brent stays near six-month highs after Houthi missile claims against Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery; Israel holds an election today. Overseas, the Nikkei rose 1.7% while Hong Kong (−0.7%) and London (−0.9%, HSBC −6%) fell. It is the heaviest earnings morning so far: beats and raised guides at SoFi, Innio, Celestica, Royal Caribbean, Johnson Controls and S&P Global; misses or weak guides at Xylem, Watsco, Commvault, Sherwin-Williams, Armstrong and HSBC; Coca-Cola beat but trades lower, Boeing's loss was wider than expected, and PayPal beat on EPS but missed on revenue. The two-day FOMC meeting starts today (decision Wednesday, hold expected; CME shows ~10% odds of a hike); the 10-year is near 4.99% and the VIX near 17.8.
